name: Rosemary Gift Nelson
feedback: D1 is outstanding. You catalogued the full set of ten canonical findings, each with a quoted source line or an exact capture timestamp and the correct OWASP plus CWE pairing: SQLi at lines 64-67 (A03/CWE-89), alg:none at lines 48-50 (A02/CWE-347), the hardcoded sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 secret (CWE-321), no exp (CWE-613), MD5 unsalted at line 66 (CWE-916), stored XSS at 02:18:47, XXE in 04-import-xxe.xml (CWE-611), path traversal at 02:24:02 (CWE-22), open redirect at 02:21:13 (CWE-601), and the cookie missing Secure and SameSite (CWE-614). The decoy is handled exactly as the key wants: you named the tempting b64url_decode helper, then proved it safe at the mechanism level (output feeds json_decode with no eval or system call, padding and strtr are RFC 4648 correct, base64_decode returns false on malformed input) and correctly pointed at alg:none, no exp, and the hardcoded secret as the real JWT bugs, so no fabrication there. D2 is strong on proof but slightly thin on the chain. Your four hops reconcile to capture lines and carry verbatim PoC, but you collapsed the chain to four hops and left stored XSS (02:18:47) and the open redirect (02:21:13) out of the ordered narrative, where the key wants hops 3 through 8 each placed in sequence. Your D2 CVSS for the SQLi uses A:H, which is too high: the auth bypass reads and writes data but does not take down availability, so the canonical vector is AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1, not 9.8 with A:H. The impact work is excellent: 312 customers, an NGN 62.4 million conservative floor with the average-balance assumption stated, and the BoltCash six-week window tied in. D3 is the highlight and reads like a real report. The executive summary is jargon-free and lands on customers and naira, the threat model names The Griot and the shared /api/v1/internal microservice, every one of the fourteen rows is grounded in evidence, the disproved decoy is restated correctly, and crucially you ordered remediation by risk-removed-per-hour of effort rather than by CVSS severity, which is exactly the discipline the brief rewards. Your two detection stopgaps are precise: a WAF rule keyed on ARGS:username with a near-zero false-positive justification, and a SIEM alert that decodes the legacy_admin_jwt cookie header and matches alg:none with a zero false-positive rationale. You also captured the senior insight that the forged super_admin token reaches the shared internal service, which is the scope change (S:C) most interns miss. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice and anchors them to your findings (the SQLi at line 64, the 312 rows in 05-exfil-sample.csv), cites ISC2 Canon 1 and Canon 4 load-bearing, and names an NDPA section tied to the PII. The one slip is that you cited Section 41 for the 72-hour NDPC notification when that 72-hour duty to the Commission is Section 40, and Section 41 is the separate duty to notify the data subjects on high risk; the section is named and correctly tied to the 312 customers, so I credited it but docked one point for the mapping. The single most important fix is to drop A:H to A:N on the SQLi CVSS and lay the chain out as the full ordered set of hops from recon through XSS and open redirect to file read, so D2 matches the rigour you already showed in D3.
